scope: Independent bounded legal-definition review for a paid personal postal order of 100 g sealed Japanese manufactured steamed/rolled/dried pure Camellia sinensis sencha. No permits, certificates, special registrations, approvals or advance notices; ordinary declaration and inspection acceptable.

manufacture.method: Official web reader full article read; direct PDF download returned403.
manufacture.finding: MAFF distinguishes primary manufacture (steaming, cooling, repeated rolling/pressure with hot air and final drying) and finishing (sorting and firing) from freshly picked leaves. Its sencha discussion gives approximately30–60 seconds steaming. This supports actual manufacture, rather than merely removing moisture from raw leaves.
manufacture.limit: General manufacturing evidence does not establish a destination exemption or a product-specific pathogen treatment validation.

ispm32.finding: Section 2 Category 1 is processing eliminating capacity for pre-processing quarantine-pest infestation; Appendix 2 explicitly includes tea. The latter is reference-only/non-prescriptive.
ispm32.legalUse: Technical commodity evidence can help apply a binding national risk-qualified definition. The standard is not itself a domestic exemption, and simple drying alone need not produce Category 1.

PM.materialNewFinding: Current Code rural L274-12 expressly imports L271-7. This is a specific statutory exception to L274-3 general exclusion of EU references. Overseas L251-2 recreated by L271-7(1°) imports Article 2(2) first-sentence plant-product definition, which covers unmanufactured products and only manufactured products capable by their nature/processing of spreading quarantine pests.

legalChain.effect: Applies Title preliminary and TitleV ChapterI to PM on L271-5 through L271-7 terms. Current page states effective14 April 2020.
Adopts living-plant definition and risk-qualified plant-product definition; latter is to be clarified by regulation. This does not adopt all EU mainland commodity schedules.
Living plants; unmanufactured products; manufactured products with relevant quarantine-pest dissemination risk; other objects also risk-qualified.

legalChain.provision: Ordinance 2019-1110 Article 5 IV/VII and Article 6 II
legalChain.effect: Creates chain above. Transitional clause retains prior law pending decree but sets14 April 2020 latest effective date. A clean assertion that the newer statute is legally uncommenced is therefore not supported.

PM.favorableInterpretation: For the stated industrially manufactured sencha, the incorporated risk-qualified definition plus the actual ISPM32 tea example provides a reasoned general-category argument for exclusion from plant-product document duties. A bespoke authority classification is not intrinsically needed. The product should not be equated to raw dried leaves simply because it remains in leaf form.

countervailingEvidence.finding: The Ministry explicitly names PM along with the other overseas territories, says the overseas decree is pending and pre-2019 law remains applicable under Article 6. This is current administrative implementation evidence directly within PM scope. Its DROM heading does not erase the named PM reference. Direct PDF retrieval failed; relevant text is from the official indexed PDF, not a successfully downloaded full PDF.

countervailingEvidence.provision: Order 483 of 28 August 2009, Arts 1–2 and 6–10, gazette printed pp106–108
countervailingEvidence.finding: Actual gazette index confirms personal/commercial post is covered and plant-products definition uses non-transformed/simple-preparation scope. The old 2010 report reproduction is a proposed text and must not alone be mistaken for enacted article numbering. No express tea classification was recovered in the enacted order.
Covered-category authorization, prior application and phytosanitary certificate duties remain. Newfoundland-only exception does not cover Japan; professional registration is not a personal-use basis.

PM.hierarchyAndLimit: An administrative instruction cannot override the statutory longstop. Conversely, treating the older local order as displaced or its simple-preparation boundary as conclusively narrowed would ignore explicit current Ministry implementation and the statute’s regulatory-clarification clause. Neither source establishes that finished sencha is prohibited, and the conflict is not a requirement to obtain a bespoke ruling.
PM.preciseRemainingGap: Resolve the publicly documented statutory/administrative implementation conflict and the applicable general manufacturing boundary for the local 2009 order. A current published general processing clarification or operative implementation text would suffice; a tea-specific permit letter is not inherently required.

WF.materialNewFinding: A full intergovernmental 2022 comparative review reproduces existing Order 95-245 Arts 2–3 in a separately labeled existing-law column. It confirms a specified prior-permit list and waiver for products outside Arts 1–2, but supplies no blanket phytosanitary-certificate waiver.

sources.provision: Existing-law column, printed pp89–90; introductory proposal-status explanation pp3–4
sources.finding: Tea is absent from the reproduced permit-required list. Article3 default waiver concerns authorization only. Proposed new biosafety sections are not enacted merely because reproduced in this report.
sources.authorityLimit: Intergovernmental secondary reproduction of existing territorial law, not an official full consolidated Order 95-245.

sources.finding: Explains 2024 revisions of invasive-species lists; seven further biosafety/import-export/quarantine sections are proposals available for future activation. Does not prove a replacement plant-product definition or manufactured-tea postal exemption.
sources.retrieval: Official indexed text read; direct download closed connection, no PDF retained.

sources.provision: GEN 1.4-4 section 1.4.2, page amendment 1 November 2014, reproduced 2026
sources.finding: Goods/mail scope, living plants and unmanufactured products, PC duty and tea-in-bulk prior permit waiver. The tea entry is specific counterevidence to reading unmanufactured alone as an unqualified manufactured-loose-tea exemption.

WF.assessment: Sencha’s processing and ISPM32 support the factual manufactured/nonliving classification. However, the explicit loose/bulk tea permit-only provision makes WF different from a jurisdiction with only a generic risk definition. A sealed retail pouch does not prove loose leaves are outside the tea-in-bulk expression. Traveller allowances do not settle mail.
WF.preciseRemainingGap: Current binding certificate scope and relation between the specific tea-in-bulk provision and unmanufactured-product definition; full current territorial plant-health consolidation or a published general manufactured-food postal rule. No contrary certificate exemption was established.
WF.notApplied: The PM/overseas L274-12 statutory chain and 2026-165 instruction were not applied to WF.

sourceAccessNotes: No repeated retrieval of inaccessible local orders after narrow failures. Failed URLs/statuses are recorded in provenance.json.
No conclusion relies on proposed SPREP 2022 text, the scientificresearch FAQ, traveller-only exemptions, or missing tea entries alone.
The contemporaneous French-definition peer independently identified the same 2019/2026 implementation conflict; its primary-reader artifacts are referenced above.
